     3	description: Use this skill for GPU training or inference clusters on SageMaker HyperPod (Slurm or

     5	  First, a GPU evidence coverage audit that proves per node whether kernel Xid logs and

     7	  found" is never reported from a silent log. Second, a node verdict (replace, reboot,

     15	metadata:
     16	  author: nzuresh
     17	  version: "1.0.3"
     18	  aws-devops-agent-skills.agent-types: "Incident RCA, Chat tasks"
     19	  aws-devops-agent-skills.aws-services: "Amazon SageMaker HyperPod, AWS ParallelCluster, Amazon EC2, Amazon FSx for Lustre, Elastic Fabric Adapter, Amazon EKS, AWS Health"
     20	  aws-devops-agent-skills.technical-domains: "Machine Learning, GenAI, High Performance Computing"
     21	---
     22	
     23	# GPU Cluster Evidence, Readiness, and Fault Verdicts
     24	
     25	For GPU clusters on SageMaker HyperPod (Slurm or EKS), AWS ParallelCluster, and self-managed
     26	EC2 or EKS. Generic investigation finds the obvious signals; this skill adds what it gets
     27	wrong: silent evidence, wrong-headline hardware verdicts, and predictable failures before a
     28	long run. **Read-only.** Never reboot, replace, update, or delete anything, and never read
     29	training data, checkpoints, or model weights.
     30	
     31	## Critical rules R1 to R10 (apply in every mode, in this order)
     32	
     33	R1. **Answer in one pass, and always leave room to answer.** In chat, do not stop to ask a
     34	   question and do not hand off to a separate investigation before answering. If an input is
     35	   missing, use the default (impact window: last 24 hours; run length: evaluate 24, 48, and
     36	   72 hours), state the assumption, and mark dependent checks `Needs input`. For "slow" or
     37	   performance questions with no time given, use the last 72 hours. Offer follow-ups only
     38	   after the answer.
     39	   **Budget the evidence gathering so the answer always gets written.** An investigation that
     40	   runs out of room before it reports is worth nothing to the operator, and it is worse than a
     41	   partial answer because it looks like a failure rather than a finding. So: collect the
     42	   mandatory evidence for the mode first (R2, R4, R5, and for Mode P the P1 to P6 core), then
     43	   write the report. Pick up the optional checks only with what is left. If you notice you are
     44	   deep into tool calls and have not yet produced an answer, **stop collecting and report what
     45	   you have**, marking everything unreached as `Not checked` with the call that would close
     46	   it. Never end a turn with evidence gathered and no verdict.
     47	R2. **Inventory and capability profile.** HyperPod: `sagemaker.DescribeCluster` and
     48	   `ListClusterNodes` (paginate). Read `NodeProvisioningMode` from `DescribeCluster`: if it is
     49	   `Continuous`, also pull `sagemaker.ListClusterEvents` for the window (see rule R11), which
     50	   is the only timeline source that survives broken log delivery. On any other value the call
     51	   is unsupported and must be skipped, not retried.
     52	   EC2/ParallelCluster/EKS: `ec2.DescribeInstances`. For every
     53	   GPU instance type: `ec2.DescribeInstanceTypes` (strip HyperPod `ml.`): GPU count,
     54	   `EfaSupported`, `MaximumEfaInterfaces`; per EC2 node, attached `efa`/`efa-only` interfaces.
     55	   Report `<attached> of <max>`, where attached = interfaces with `InterfaceType` `efa` or
     56	   `efa-only` (the primary ENA interface does not count unless it is `efa`). HyperPod nodes
     57	   are not visible to `DescribeInstances`: say so. On NVSwitch types, search every log source
     58	   found under rule R4 for `Started "Nvidia Fabric Manager"` before saying it is not confirmed.
     59	R3. **Node identity survives replacement.** A HyperPod reboot keeps the instance ID; a replace
     60	   gives the node a **new instance ID in the same instance group**, so the current ID will
     61	   never appear in the replace request. Query CloudTrail **by event name, not by instance
     62	   ID**: `cloudtrail.LookupEvents` with `LookupAttributes=[{AttributeKey: EventName,
     63	   AttributeValue: BatchReplaceClusterNodes}]`, then again for `BatchRebootClusterNodes`,
     64	   `BatchDeleteClusterNodes`, and `UpdateCluster`, with `StartTime` = window start minus 6
     65	   hours and `EndTime` = now as full ISO-8601 UTC timestamps, paginating with `NextToken`.
     66	   Keep events whose `requestParameters.clusterName` is this cluster. A `nodeIds` entry
     67	   that is not in the current `ListClusterNodes` output was replaced; the instance group
     68	   whose node has a `LaunchTime` just after that event is the replaced group. That operator
     69	   or automatic call is the explanation for the node going `Pending` (Branch E), not hardware.
     70	R4. **Find every log source by substring, not prefix.** Call `logs.DescribeLogGroups` with
     71	   `logGroupNamePattern` (case-sensitive substring) = the cluster name, then again for
     72	   `kernel`, `messages`, `syslog`, `journal`, and `gpu`, paginating with `nextToken`. Never
     73	   search only `/aws/parallelcluster` or `/aws/sagemaker` prefixes: customer pipelines use
     74	   other names (for example `/aws/<pipeline>/<cluster>/kernel`). Evaluate every source found.
     75	R5. **Prove coverage before any "no errors".** For each node and source: find the stream that
     76	   carries `kernel:` lines, then bin **that exact stream** by hour across the window padded by
     77	   one hour. **Always name the evidence you used: quote the full log group name and the exact
     78	   log stream name for every node in the coverage table, and again in the answer text.** A
     79	   coverage claim without the group and stream it rests on is not auditable, so the operator
     80	   cannot re-run it. Any empty hour means `Not observable` for that hour. First and last event times
     81	   are not proof, and the time of the **last `kernel:` line** is not when logging stopped:
     82	   a healthy kernel goes quiet. Liveness comes only from the hourly bins of all lines in
     83	   that stream. A node is `Measured` if one source passes. HyperPod: a missing
     84	   `SagemakerHealthMonitoringAgent/<group>/<instance-id>` stream means `No HMA detections`
     85	   when the cluster log group is otherwise live. NCCL transport with no `NCCL INFO` lines
     86	   anywhere is `Not observable`; never infer it from the instance type.
     87	R5a. **Name every resource you looked at, by ID.** A finding the operator cannot re-run is
     88	   not a finding. Whatever you analysed, put its identifier in the answer: the FSx file system
     89	   (`fs-...`) behind any storage claim, the instance IDs (`i-...`) behind any node claim, the
     90	   cluster name, the capacity reservation (`cr-...`) behind any capacity claim, and the log
     91	   group and stream behind any log claim as R5 already requires. "The file system was
     92	   saturated" or "the metrics looked fine" names nothing and cannot be checked. This applies
     93	   to the resource you cleared as much as the one you blamed, since ruling something out is
     94	   only useful if the reader knows what was ruled out.
     95	R6. **Verdict per node, headline to match.** `REPLACE`, `REBOOT`, `LEAVE ALONE`, `MONITOR`, or
     96	   `NOT OBSERVABLE`, against the evidence bar in `references/incident-branches.md` (Step 4b).
     97	   Application-class Xids (for example 13, 31) or HMA `reason: XidUserAppError` with the node
     98	   `Running` is `LEAVE ALONE`. Never headline "hardware error" unless the verdict is `REPLACE`
     99	   or `REBOOT` on hardware grounds.
     100	R7. **Label every cause** `Proven` (measured signal on the affected node, before the failure,
     101	   nothing competing) or `Hypothesis (to validate)` with the one confirming measurement. A
     102	   spike at the same time is correlation. FSx without a saturated metric is not a proven cause.
     103	   Only a `Proven` cause may be called the root cause, in the headline or in a branch table.
     104	   Otherwise write `Leading hypothesis: <cause>`, or `Root cause: Not observable` when the
     105	   deciding evidence is missing (for example a dead control-plane log). Never write "Proven
     106	   mechanism" for something whose trigger or removal path you did not observe.
     107	   Utilization metrics from FSx (`NetworkThroughputUtilization`, `DiskIopsUtilization`, and
     108	   similar) and `GPUPowerUtilization` are already percent from 0 to 100: a value of `0.9` is
     109	   0.9 percent. Quote the raw value with a percent sign.
     110	R8. **Recovery questions** always state three things: whether automatic node recovery is on
     111	   (`NodeRecovery`), what it does (reboot or replace the node), and that the **job** resumes
     112	   only with checkpoints plus the orchestrator's auto-resume (Slurm on HyperPod:
     113	   `srun --auto-resume=1`).
     114	R9. **Capacity Blocks** begin terminating instances 30 minutes before the end time (60 for
     115	   UltraServers); blocks end at 11:30 UTC and termination starts at 11:00 UTC on the last day.
     116	   For a planned run, write out: usable until = end time minus the lead time; run end = start
     117	   plus run length; hours covered = usable until minus start. Give every value as a full UTC
     118	   date and time, and check the latest safe start is not already in the past.
     119	R10. **Rule out the frequent non-GPU causes** in `references/cluster-edge-cases.md` before
     120	   blaming hardware: subnet IP or network interface exhaustion, ParallelCluster bootstrap
     121	   failures and protected mode, EFA nodes in a public subnet, a Capacity Block not yet
     122	   active, and the FSx maintenance window. HyperPod does not export system metrics to
     123	   CloudWatch, so HyperPod GPU activity is `Not observable` there.
     124	R11. **When the logs are dead, ask the control plane.** On a HyperPod cluster with
     125	   `NodeProvisioningMode = Continuous`, `sagemaker.ListClusterEvents` gives you a node and
     126	   cluster timeline that owes nothing to a log agent, so it keeps answering when a stream has
     127	   gone silent or a node has disappeared. Filter the window with `EventTimeAfter` and
     128	   `EventTimeBefore`, narrow with `NodeId` or `InstanceGroupName`, sort with
     129	   `SortBy=EventTime`, and page through `NextToken`. Where a `Description` is not
     130	   self-explanatory, `DescribeClusterEvent` has the detail. Note that the response has no
     131	   severity or level field at all, so any grouping you apply is your own and should be
     132	   described that way. If `NodeProvisioningMode` is anything other than `Continuous` the call
     133	   is not supported; write `ListClusterEvents not supported` in the coverage table and carry
     134	   on. What you must not do is report a dead log as "no events" without either trying this
     135	   source or saying it was unavailable.
     136	
     137	## Pick the mode
     138	
     139	| The user asks | Mode | Steps to run |
     140	|---------------|------|--------------|
     141	| Something failed, hung, slowed, or lost nodes | **I: Incident** | Steps 1 to 7 |
     142	| "Were there GPU errors?", "Can I trust the logs?" | **C: Coverage audit** | Steps 1 to 3, then 6 and 7 |
     143	| "Is the cluster ready for a long run?", Capacity Block ending | **P: Pre-flight** | Steps 1 to 3, then 5P, 6 and 7 |
     144	
     145	## Workflow checklist
     146	
     147	Work through these in order and tick each one as it completes. Skip only the steps the
     148	mode table excludes. Every step below has a matching `## Step N` section with its detail.
     149	
     150	- [ ] Step 1: Scope the request: account, region, cluster or instance IDs, impact window
     151	- [ ] Step 2: Build the inventory, capability profile, and one ordered timeline
     152	- [ ] Step 3: Prove GPU log coverage per node before looking for errors
     153	- [ ] Step 4: Classify each fault and give every node a verdict
     154	- [ ] Step 5: Pull metrics and settle the root-cause branch
     155	- [ ] Step 5P: Score pre-flight checks P1 to P16 (Mode P only, replaces Steps 4 and 5)
     156	- [ ] Step 6: Write the report in the required format
     157	- [ ] Step 7: Self-check the finished output, then present it
     158	
     159	## Step 1: Scope
     160	
     161	Account, region, cluster name or instance IDs, workload, impact window (default last 24 hours,
     162	stated). Classify the symptom to pick a starting branch (Step 5), but collect evidence for all.
     163	
     164	## Step 2: Inventory and timeline
     165	
     166	Load [references/inventory-and-timeline.md](references/inventory-and-timeline.md) for the
     167	inventory API calls and the eight timeline sources, and
     168	[references/cluster-edge-cases.md](references/cluster-edge-cases.md) for the frequent non-GPU
     169	causes to rule out under rule R10:
     170	
     171	```
     172	read_skill_resource(skill_id="aiml-gpu-training-cluster-investigation", path="references/inventory-and-timeline.md")
     173	read_skill_resource(skill_id="aiml-gpu-training-cluster-investigation", path="references/cluster-edge-cases.md")
     174	```
     175	
     176	Build one ordered timeline for the window plus 30 minutes each side: node state, HMA
     177	detections, Xids, AWS Health, EC2 status and scheduled events, Capacity Block and training plan
     178	end times, and CloudTrail cluster changes (rule R3).
     179	
     180	## Step 3: Coverage audit
     181	
     182	Load [references/coverage-audit.md](references/coverage-audit.md) for the log-source discovery
     183	and hourly coverage queries, and
     184	[references/nccl-nvlink-efa.md](references/nccl-nvlink-efa.md) for NCCL transport, NVLink and
     185	NVSwitch, and EFA signals:
     186	
     187	```
     188	read_skill_resource(skill_id="aiml-gpu-training-cluster-investigation", path="references/coverage-audit.md")
     189	read_skill_resource(skill_id="aiml-gpu-training-cluster-investigation", path="references/nccl-nvlink-efa.md")
     190	```
     191	
     192	Produce the coverage table and the node capability and fabric table for every affected node.
     193	Every row names the full log group name and the exact log stream name that row's verdict rests
     194	on, so the operator can re-run the same query. Where no stream carries kernel lines, say which
     195	groups you searched and that none did.
     196	
     197	## Step 4: Classify faults and give node verdicts
     198	
     199	Load [references/xid-triage.md](references/xid-triage.md) for the Xid catalog and per-code
     200	verdicts, and [references/incident-branches.md](references/incident-branches.md) for the node
     201	verdict evidence bar and branches A to F:
     202	
     203	```
     204	read_skill_resource(skill_id="aiml-gpu-training-cluster-investigation", path="references/xid-triage.md")
     205	read_skill_resource(skill_id="aiml-gpu-training-cluster-investigation", path="references/incident-branches.md")
     206	```
     207	
     208	## Step 5: Metrics and root-cause branch
     209	
     210	Load [references/signals-and-thresholds.md](references/signals-and-thresholds.md) for metric
     211	names, dimensions, and thresholds:
     212	
     213	```
     214	read_skill_resource(skill_id="aiml-gpu-training-cluster-investigation", path="references/signals-and-thresholds.md")
     215	```
     216	
     217	Pull FSx (correct dimensions per metric), GPU activity (`AWS/EC2` `GPUPowerUtilization`, unit
     218	Percent, or `CWAgent`), and EFA counters, then evaluate branches A (hardware), B (capacity
     219	lifecycle), C (storage), D (NCCL, NVLink/NVSwitch, EFA), E (cluster change), and F (application,
     220	only after A to E are ruled out), as defined in `incident-branches.md`. Recommend operator
     221	actions only.
     222	
     223	## Step 5P: Pre-flight readiness (Mode P)
     224	
     225	Load [references/preflight.md](references/preflight.md) for pre-flight checks P1 to P16:
     226	
     227	```
     228	read_skill_resource(skill_id="aiml-gpu-training-cluster-investigation", path="references/preflight.md")
     229	```
     230	
     231	Score checks P1 to P16. Lead with FAIL, then RISK. In Mode P this step replaces
     232	Steps 4 and 5.
     233	
     234	**Work the core first, then extend.** All sixteen checks together cost more tool calls than
     235	a single answer usually has room for, and a readiness question with no verdict is a failed
     236	answer however much evidence sits behind it (see R1). So run them in two passes.
     237	
     238	The core, which decides whether the run can start at all:
     239	
     240	| Check | Question it settles |
     241	|-------|---------------------|
     242	| P1 | Does the Capacity Block or training plan outlast the run? |
     243	| P2 | Is there an extension, if it does not? |
     244	| P3 | Is there a spare node to replace a failure? |
     245	| P4 | Is `NodeRecovery` on? |
     246	| P5 | Are deep health checks enabled? |
     247	| P6 | Is GPU error logging arriving, so a failure during the run is visible? |
     248	
     249	Write the readiness verdict as soon as those six are scored. P7 to P16 then refine it, and
     250	each one you reach can only add a `RISK`, never change a `FAIL` already found in the core.
     251	Anything you do not reach is reported `Not checked` with the call that would settle it, which
     252	is an honest answer; silence is not. If the core itself is incomplete, say which part and
     253	give the verdict you can support.
     254	
     255	## Step 6: Report
     256	
     257	Load [references/report-format.md](references/report-format.md) for the report template and its rules:
     258	
     259	```
     260	read_skill_resource(skill_id="aiml-gpu-training-cluster-investigation", path="references/report-format.md")
     261	```
     262	
     263	## Step 7: Self-check before presenting
     264	
     265	Before showing the answer to the user, re-read your own draft and verify each of these.
     266	Fix the draft where a check fails; do not present an output that fails one.
     267	
     268	- [ ] Every "no errors found" statement is backed by a node whose coverage you proved in
     269	      Step 3. If coverage was not proven, the wording is `Not observable`, not healthy.
     270	- [ ] Every coverage row names its full log group and exact log stream (rule R5). A coverage
     271	      claim with no named source is not auditable and must be fixed before presenting.
     272	- [ ] Every node verdict still meets the evidence bar that justifies it, re-read from
     273	      [references/incident-branches.md](references/incident-branches.md) Step 4b.
     274	- [ ] The headline matches the verdicts. It does not say "hardware error" unless a verdict
     275	      is `REPLACE` or `REBOOT` on hardware grounds (rule R6).
     276	- [ ] Every cause carries a `Proven` or `Hypothesis (to validate)` label, and anything
     277	      labelled `Proven` has a measured signal on the affected node before the failure
     278	      (rule R7). Nothing unproven is called the root cause.
     279	- [ ] Every percentage came straight from the metric without rescaling (rule R7).
     280	- [ ] Every absent signal is reported as `Not observable` with what to collect, never as
     281	      zero or as healthy.
     282	- [ ] Each recommendation names an operator action, and no mutating API call was made.
     283	- [ ] Every number in the answer can be traced to a call you actually made this run.
     284	- [ ] Every resource you analysed appears by ID (rule R5a): the `fs-...` behind a storage
     285	      claim, the `i-...` behind a node claim, the `cr-...` behind a capacity claim, the
     286	      cluster name, the log group and stream. This holds for resources you cleared, not just
     287	      the one you blamed.
     288	- [ ] **There is an actual answer.** A verdict or root cause is written down, not just
     289	      evidence. If you ran out of room before finishing, the draft still leads with the
     290	      verdict you can support and marks the rest `Not checked` (rule R1).
     291	
     292	State the outcome of this self-check in one line, naming anything you could not verify.
     293	
     294	## Success criteria
     295	
     296	- Coverage table and node capability table for every affected node; no "no errors" without
     297	  proven coverage.
     298	- One verdict per node with a GPU signal; headline consistent with the verdicts.
     299	- Every cause labelled `Proven` or `Hypothesis (to validate)`.
     300	- Replaced nodes matched to the operator or automatic action that replaced them.
     301	- Mode P: P1 to P16 scored.
     302	- No mutating API call was made.

     15	| Node in `Pending` | Longer than 30 minutes: replacement or launch blocked. Check capacity and `LifecycleConfig` logs. |
     16	| Node in `DeepHealthCheckInProgress` | Well past 2 hours. DCGM level 4 alone typically takes about 45 to 90 minutes, and the stress, EFA, and NCCL tests add to it. Check `DeepHealthCheckResults/<id>` streams first |
     17	| `CurrentCount < TargetCount` | Persisting across two inventory reads. |
     18	| `NodeRecovery = None` | Always report. Automatic reboot or replace is disabled. |
     19	| `CurrentImageId != DesiredImageId` | Software update in progress or stalled. |

     21	## FSx for Lustre (`AWS/FSx`)
     22	
     23	Metric semantics and dimensions:
     24	[FSx for Lustre metrics and dimensions](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/fsx/latest/LustreGuide/fs-metrics.html).
     25	
     26	| Metric (dimensions) | Stat | Flag when | Meaning |
     27	|---------------------|------|-----------|---------|
     28	| `NetworkThroughputUtilization` (FileSystemId, FileServer) | Maximum | ≥ 90% sustained 5+ min | File server network throughput saturated |
     29	| `FileServerDiskThroughputUtilization` (FileSystemId, FileServer) | Maximum | ≥ 90% sustained 5+ min | OSS-to-disk throughput saturated |
     30	| `DiskIopsUtilization` (FileSystemId, StorageTargetId) | Maximum | ≥ 90% sustained 5+ min | OST IOPS saturated (not on Scratch or Persistent HDD) |
     31	| `CPUUtilization` (FileSystemId, FileServer = MDS*) | Maximum | ≥ 90% sustained 5+ min | Metadata server saturated |

{"id": "52a6d450-eedc-45ca-955f-b0b745fd7858", "role": "user", "content": [{"id": "tooluse_zzdkpwhcvIO6fIQzmqIWvw", "content": [{"text": "     1	# NCCL Transport, NVLink / NVSwitch, and EFA Signals
     2	
     3	Where each GPU-communication signal can be seen, what a good and a bad value look like,
     4	and what to do when it is not visible. Log strings are quoted from the sources linked in
     5	each section. Do not paraphrase them into search patterns that match more than they say.
     6	
     7	## 1. Which transport NCCL actually used
     8	
     9	NCCL writes its transport choices only when `NCCL_DEBUG=INFO` (or higher) is set, and only
     10	to the job's stdout or to `NCCL_DEBUG_FILE`. These reach CloudWatch only if the customer
     11	ships job output. Search every log source found in SKILL.md Step 3a for `NCCL INFO` and
     12	`NCCL WARN` first. **If there are no NCCL lines at all, NCCL transport is `Not observable`.**
     13	Never infer "NCCL used EFA" from the instance type or the EFA security group.
     14	
     15	| Log line | Meaning | Verdict |
     16	|----------|---------|---------|
     17	| `NET/OFI Selected Provider is efa` and `Using network AWS Libfabric` | Inter-node traffic goes over EFA through the AWS OFI NCCL plugin | Good |
     18	| `Using network IB` | NCCL chose an InfiniBand-verbs network | Unexpected on EC2 EFA instances; report it |
     19	| Channel lines `... via NET/Socket/<n>` | Inter-node traffic over TCP sockets | **Bad** on EFA instances: silent fallback. The AWS blog on P3dn measured about a three-fold bus-bandwidth gain for EFA over TCP |
     20	| Channel lines `... via P2P/CUMEM` | Intra-node GPU to GPU by direct peer access (NVLink on NVSwitch nodes) | Good |
     21	| `NVLS Creating Multicast group ...` | NVLink SHARP in use for collectives | Good on NVSwitch systems that support it |
     22	| Channel lines `... via SHM/direct/direct` | Intra-node traffic through host shared memory | On an NVSwitch node, peer access is not being used; report as degraded |
     23	
     24	Sources: [NCCL logging](https://docs.nvidia.com/deeplearning/nccl/user-guide/docs/troubleshooting/logging.html),
     25	[Training LLMs on SageMaker: best practices](https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/machine-learning/training-large-language-models-on-amazon-sagemaker-best-practices/),
     26	[Optimizing deep learning on P3dn with EFA](https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/compute/optimizing-deep-learning-on-p3-and-p3dn-with-efa/).
     27	
     28	When NCCL is not observable, give the operator this to collect on one affected job:
     29	`NCCL_DEBUG=INFO NCCL_DEBUG_SUBSYS=INIT,NET,P2P,SHM,NVLS NCCL_DEBUG_FILE=/fsx/nccl_%h_%p.log`
     30	(subsystem names from the NCCL logging page), then search the files for the lines above.
     31	
     32	## 2. NVLink and NVSwitch fabric
     33	
     34	The CloudWatch agent's NVIDIA plugin does **not** collect any NVLink counter (its full
     35	metric list is utilization, temperature, power, memory, PCIe link, encoder, and clocks).
     36	NVLink health reaches AWS only through the system log:
     37	
     38	| Signal | Where | Meaning |
     39	|--------|-------|---------|
     40	| `NVRM: Xid ...: 74` | Kernel log, HyperPod HMA | NVLink error (NVIDIA catalog: immediate action per NVLink workflow, investigatory action contact support). Hardware class |
     41	| `NVRM: Xid ...: 71`, `NVLink: fatal error detected on link <n>` | Kernel log, HyperPod HMA (`reason: XidHardwareFailure`) | Fatal NVLink error; example in the HyperPod HMA documentation. Hardware class |
     42	| `NVRM: Xid ...: 155` / `156` | Kernel log | GPU NVLink flit CRC error / lane error (listed by Amazon ECS GPU auto repair). Hardware class |
     43	| Other `NVRM:` lines that mention NVLink without `Xid` | Kernel log | Driver diagnostics. List them in the timeline with node and hour. **Do not classify** them or call them a cause without corroboration |
     44	| Fabric Manager start: `Started "Nvidia Fabric Manager"` | System log (`/var/log/messages` or journal) | Fabric Manager service started. Applies to NVSwitch instance types (section 4) |
     45	| `CX Bridge device ... is usable for NVLink subnet management` | System log | P6-B200 and P6-B300 only: AWS documents that on these types Fabric Manager configures NVFabric through ConnectX bridge devices, so this line shows the bridge was found |
     46	| Fabric Manager absent, failed, or restarting on an NVSwitch instance | System log | NVLink between GPUs may not be up. Hardware or driver-stack problem: node verdict `REBOOT`, then `REPLACE` if it recurs. AWS documents Fabric Manager as required on P6-B200 and P6-B300; on other NVSwitch types, report a failure as a strong signal but label the NVLink impact `Hypothesis (to validate)` with `nvidia-smi topo -m` as the check |
     47	| `nvidia-fabricmanager.service: ... PIDFile= references a path below legacy directory /var/run/` | System log | systemd path warning. **Benign.** Exclude it before counting Fabric Manager "errors" |
     48	
     49	Sources: [NVIDIA Xid catalog](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/xid-errors/analyzing-xid-catalog.html),
     50	[HyperPod health monitoring](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/sagemaker-hyperpod-eks-resiliency-health-monitoring-agent.html),
     51	[ECS GPU auto repair Xid list](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonECS/latest/developerguide/managed-instances-gpu-auto-repair.html),
     52	[EC2 public NVIDIA drivers, P6-B200 and P6-B300 considerations](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/public-nvidia-driver.html),
     53	[CloudWatch agent NVIDIA metrics](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/monitoring/CloudWatch-Agent-NVIDIA-GPU.html).
     54	
     55	On-node confirmation for the operator (not available through AWS APIs): NVLink status and
     56	error counters from `nvidia-smi nvlink` and DCGM, and `systemctl status nvidia-fabricmanager`.
     57	
     58	### On-node NVLink and fabric fields, captured from a live p6-b300.48xlarge
     59	
     60	Taken from a node running driver 595.91.07 and CUDA 13.2 with 8 x `NVIDIA B300 SXM6 AC`.
     61	Quote these names as they appear. This is the operator-side evidence behind the NVLink 5
     62	family, Xid 144 to 150, in `references/xid-triage.md` rule 10.
     63	
     64	| Command | Healthy reading observed | How to read it |
     65	|---------|--------------------------|----------------|
     66	| `nvidia-smi nvlink -s` | `Link <n>: 53.125 GB/s` for every link | A link that is missing, or reads `<inactive>`, is down. Compare the link count across all 8 GPUs; an asymmetry is the fault location |
     67	| `nvidia-smi nvlink -e` | All zero: `Malformed packet Errors`, `Buffer overrun Errors`, `Rx Errors`, `Rx remote Errors`, `Rx General Errors`, `Local link integrity Errors`, `Tx discards`, `Link recovery successful events`, `Link recovery failed events`, `Total link recovery events`, `Effective Errors`, `Symbol Errors` | These are the exact counter names on driver 595.91.07. Non-zero on one link on one GPU points at that link, and these are the counters to quote when an Xid 144 to 150 names a link. `Link recovery failed events` above zero is the strongest of them. Note the older `Replay Errors` / `Recovery Errors` / `CRC Errors` names are **not** present on this driver, so do not look for them |
     68	| `nvidia-smi nvlink -e`, FEC fields | `FEC Errors - 0: <large and growing>`, buckets 1 to 15 at or near `0` | **Do not report bucket 0 as an error count.** It is the corrected-codeword counter and reads in the billions on a healthy link (36,140,749,276 observed at boot). Only buckets climbing above 0 indicate real link stress |
     69	| `nvidia-smi nvlink -e`, BER fields | `Effective BER: 15e-255`, `Symbol BER: 15e-255` | `15e-255` is the floating-point floor, meaning effectively zero. Do not read it as a large exponent or a high error rate |
     70	| `nvidia-smi nvlink -e`, raw lane fields | `Raw BER Lane 0: 2061`, `Raw BER Lane 1: 1038`, `Raw BER Total: 1037`, `Raw Errors Lane 0: 82`, `Raw Errors Lane 1: 4` | **All of these were non-zero on a healthy node at boot.** They are pre-correction physical-layer counters, so a non-zero value is normal and is not a fault. Never report `Raw Errors` or `Raw BER` as evidence of an NVLink problem on its own. Use them only as a trend against the same link's earlier reading, and lead with the corrected counters above |
     71	| `nvidia-smi -q`, `Fabric` section | `State: Completed`, `Status: Success`, `CliqueId: 0`, plus a per-GPU `GPU Fabric GUID` | `State` other than `Completed` or `Status` other than `Success` means the GPU has not joined the NVLink fabric. This is the single clearest fabric health field, better than parsing Fabric Manager log lines |
     72	| `systemctl is-active nvidia-fabricmanager` | `active` | Anything else on an NVSwitch type is a REBOOT candidate per the table above |
     73	| `nvidia-smi topo -m` | `NV18` between every GPU pair | `NV18` means 18 bonded NVLinks. A pair reading `SYS` or `PHB` instead has lost NVLink and fell back to PCIe or the host interconnect, which is the topology-level version of the SHM fallback in section 1 |
     74	
     75	Two things to watch for, both seen on the healthy node above. The FEC bucket-0 counter and
     76	the `15e-255` BER floor both look alarming at a glance and neither is a fault, so calling
     77	either one an error is simply wrong. Separately, `dmesg` on a healthy node carries
     78	`NVRM: API mismatch` warnings whenever a userspace component lags the kernel module
     79	version; `nvidia-gridd` did exactly that here. Filter those out before you count NVRM
     80	errors, the same way you would drop the Fabric Manager `PIDFile=` warning.
     81	
     82	## 3. EFA error counters
     83

**Is storage, the network, or the GPUs responsible for the throughput drop? None of them.** The `distributed-training-triage-b200` cluster had **zero GPU compute nodes for the entire window** — a **capacity-lifecycle** problem, not a storage, network, or GPU-hardware fault.

# Investigation Summary

## Symptoms

### B200 training throughput drop
**Description:** Training throughput for the B200 benchmark job has degraded over the last few days. Impact window defaults to the last 72 hours (2026-09-28T04:08Z to 2026-10-01T04:08Z) as no specific start time was given. Root cause not yet isolated among storage (FSx for Lustre), network (EFA/NCCL), or GPU utilization.
**Time:** 2026-09-28T04:08:00Z - 2026-10-01T04:08:00Z

## Findings

### Cause: GPU compute fleet may have already been gone before the reported slowdown window
**Description:** CONFIRMED via direct EC2 describe_instances + describe_capacity_reservations calls: the target cluster's GPU workers (i-0be6193831c898671, i-0014ff22f2e2f180f) ran normally from 2026-09-23T16:06Z and were terminated at exactly 2026-09-27T11:00:00Z (classic Capacity Block expiry signature) — roughly 17 hours before the impact window (2026-09-28T04:08Z) even began. No target-cluster GPU worker has existed since. The sole replacement p6-b300 Capacity Block (cr-0580a9d7420fd589a, TotalInstanceCount=1, AvailableInstanceCount=0, active 2026-09-30T11:30Z→2026-10-03T11:30Z, us-west-2b) has its only slot occupied by an unrelated Blackwell-verification node (i-0ec31e7eff7635265, different VPC vpc-0968395d1c4c18fbc, tagged Purpose=PR112-blackwell-verification, no parallelcluster tag). The target cluster distributed-training-triage-b200 has therefore had ZERO available GPU capacity for the entire impact window through now.
**Cascades to:** symptom-training-throughput-drop

#### Supporting Observations
- **GPU compute fleet was already terminated before the impact window began:** The target cluster's GPU compute fleet was absent for most of the impact window. The two prior GPU workers (i-0be6193831c898671, i-0014ff22f2e2f180f) terminated at exactly 2026-09-27T11:00:00Z - a classic Capacity Block termination signature - approximately 17 hours before the impact window (2026-09-28T04:08Z-2026-10-01T04:08Z) even began. No GPU workers ran from 2026-09-28T04:08Z through 2026-09-30T21:44Z, covering roughly 65% of the window. A new node, i-0ec31e7eff7635265, launched 2026-09-30T21:44:50Z on capacity block cr-0580a9d7420fd589a, but it ships ZERO logs to any CloudWatch log group - this is a telemetry coverage gap, not confirmation the node is healthy. That node also has only a standard ENA network interface attached (0 of 16 possible EFA interfaces) - flagged as an unconfirmed precondition concern rather than fact, since this is a single-node reservation where inter-node EFA may not even be required. Both HyperPod clusters in the account were ruled out earlier (different subnet, different instance types); head nodes for both ParallelCluster stacks remain healthy throughout.
- **7 historical GPU worker instances discovered via CloudWatch metric dimensions:** AWS/EC2 namespace GPUPowerUtilization metric dimension-listing revealed 7 instance IDs that were GPU training nodes for this cluster even though none are running now: i-0a3cfc5c0505eb807, i-0190035035290b380, i-01ec042d2f0e3e7fb, i-0ce092c23d7562556, i-0014ff22f2e2f180f, i-0be6193831c898671 (all with GpuId dimension 1-8, standard 8-GPU B300 nodes), and i-0ec31e7eff7635265 (uses UUID-style GpuId values, 7 GPUs seen — this is the SEPARATE 'b300-xid-verify' instance in a different VPC, already flagged as unrelated to this cluster, so effectively 6 real worker nodes for this job). CWAgent namespace has NO nvidia_smi/EFA metrics published — only mem/disk percent on an unrelated instance — so GPU utilization and EFA counters cannot be read via CWAgent; AWS/EC2 built-in GPU metrics are the only available source. Critically, initial GetMetricData queries for GPUPowerUtilization (both at InstanceId-only dimension and InstanceId+GpuId dimension, hourly period, window 2026-09-27 to 2026-10-01) returned ZERO datapoints — this needs further investigation (could mean metrics aren't emitted at that period/stat, instances terminated before window, or a dimension/parameter issue) and is not yet a confirmed finding of 'GPUs idle.'

#### Gaps
- **CloudTrail blocked — cannot recover historical GPU worker instance IDs:** CloudTrail lookup_events (RunInstances/TerminateInstances) is not permitted in this environment ('cloudtrail service operations are not allowed'). Since no GPU compute nodes are currently running in the target VPC, this is the only way to recover the instance IDs of the GPU workers that ran during the impact window (2026-09-28T04:08Z–2026-10-01T04:08Z). Without those IDs, the GPU/EFA/NCCL telemetry subagents cannot query CloudWatch for the relevant historical GPU utilization, EFA, or NCCL metrics — this is a hard blocker on the compute and network branches of the investigation. (Note: the AWS Health API required the us-east-1 global endpoint — regional calls failed — but once called correctly it returned zero events in-window; that was a transient tool-use issue, not itself a gap.)

### Root Cause: Capacity lifecycle: target cluster has had zero available GPU capacity since 2026-09-27T11:00Z
**Description:** ROOT CAUSE: The training cluster distributed-training-triage-b200 lost its reserved GPU capacity when its prior Capacity Block expired (GPU workers i-0be6193831c898671 and i-0014ff22f2e2f180f terminated at exactly 2026-09-27T11:00:00Z — ~17h before the impact window began) and has been unable to reacquire GPU capacity since: the sole replacement p6-b300 Capacity Block (cr-0580a9d7420fd589a, TotalInstanceCount=1, AvailableInstanceCount=0, active 2026-09-30T11:30Z→2026-10-03T11:30Z, us-west-2b, account 111122223333) has its only slot held by an unrelated Blackwell-verification node (i-0ec31e7eff7635265, 'b300-xid-verify', different VPC vpc-0968395d1c4c18fbc, Purpose=PR112-blackwell-verification, no parallelcluster tag, 0 EFA interfaces). A cluster with zero GPU workers cannot make training progress — this fully explains the reported throughput collapse over 'the last few days'. This is proven/measured via EC2 instance lifecycle data, capacity reservation state, CloudWatch log-stream lifecycle (GPU kernel/system-messages streams ending exactly at the termination timestamp), and FSx client-count corroboration (ClientConnections constant at 1 — only the head node ever mounted the filesystem). Storage (FSx), GPU hardware, and network (NCCL/EFA/NVLink) were independently investigated and are not the cause: FSx never approached saturation, and zero Xid/NCCL/Fabric-Manager faults were found on any node that was logging during its active period.
**Cascades to:** hyp-fleet-terminated-before-window

#### Supporting Observations
- **GPU compute fleet was already terminated before the impact window began:** The target cluster's GPU compute fleet was absent for most of the impact window. The two prior GPU workers (i-0be6193831c898671, i-0014ff22f2e2f180f) terminated at exactly 2026-09-27T11:00:00Z - a classic Capacity Block termination signature - approximately 17 hours before the impact window (2026-09-28T04:08Z-2026-10-01T04:08Z) even began. No GPU workers ran from 2026-09-28T04:08Z through 2026-09-30T21:44Z, covering roughly 65% of the window. A new node, i-0ec31e7eff7635265, launched 2026-09-30T21:44:50Z on capacity block cr-0580a9d7420fd589a, but it ships ZERO logs to any CloudWatch log group - this is a telemetry coverage gap, not confirmation the node is healthy. That node also has only a standard ENA network interface attached (0 of 16 possible EFA interfaces) - flagged as an unconfirmed precondition concern rather than fact, since this is a single-node reservation where inter-node EFA may not even be required. Both HyperPod clusters in the account were ruled out earlier (different subnet, different instance types); head nodes for both ParallelCluster stacks remain healthy throughout.
- **Head-node control-plane logs stopped shipping before impact window; no evidence of GPU fleet launch during window:** Fault-search results across available logs (2026-09-26 to 2026-10-01): zero NVRM Xid lines found across 765K+ scanned records in the kernel log group and 135K scanned records in the ParallelCluster log group. Zero NCCL lines found anywhere. Fabric Manager lines were found only on an unrelated AMI-build host (ip-172-31-0-64, outside the cluster's VPC/subnets), consisting of benign startup warnings with no failures. Separately, the head node's own scheduler logs are dead well before the impact window: slurmctld has not shipped since 2026-08-27, and clustermgtd/clustermgtd_events/clusterstatusmgtd have not shipped since 2026-08-31 - both roughly a month before the impact window started. This means the scheduler's own record of why/how the GPU fleet was terminated on 2026-09-27 is NOT OBSERVABLE, not necessarily absent - the logs needed to check are simply not being shipped during the relevant period. The head node's live kernel stream during the window is dominated by a benign systemd user-session login/logout loop (~4,392 cycles), not scheduler activity.
- **GPU power utilization near-idle across all observable nodes:** Across all 7 instances that ever published AWS/EC2 GPUPowerUtilization data between 2026-09-23 and 2026-10-01, every GPU stayed far below the 5% activity threshold (raw percent, Unit="None"). The 4 oldest nodes (i-0a3cfc5c0505eb807, i-0190035035290b380, i-01ec042d2f0e3e7fb, i-0ce092c23d7562556) only have data on 2026-09-23, near-zero (0-0.08%). The two in-cluster worker nodes (i-0014ff22f2e2f180f, i-0be6193831c898671) show a brief synchronized bump to ~0.5% raw on 09-24 across all 8 GPUs, then flat near-idle ~0.005-0.02% through 09-27, with all GPUs moving in lockstep (no straggler). The only node with data strictly inside the impact window (2026-09-28T04:08Z-2026-10-01T04:08Z) is i-0ec31e7eff7635265 (09-30 21:08Z onward): hourly Maximum pins at a flat 1.0% raw per-sample ceiling, but hourly Average is only 0.04-0.17% raw across its 7 GPUs - essentially idle, no decline, no straggler divergence. IMPORTANT CAVEAT: i-0ec31e7eff7635265 was separately confirmed by the cluster-inventory subagent to live in a DIFFERENT VPC (vpc-0968395d1c4c18fbc, named "b300-xid-verify") and is NOT part of the target distributed-training-triage-b200 cluster - so its data should not be attributed to the investigated training job; it is included here only for completeness since it was the only node with any in-window GPU metric data.

## Other Gaps

### EFA network counters and GPU memory not observable
**Description:** CloudWatch CWAgent namespace contains no efa_* metrics and no nvidia_smi_* metrics on any GPU worker instance - only mem_used_percent/disk_used_percent on an unrelated instance (i-08a11867e0b7e311d). This means Branch D (NCCL/EFA network fabric) and GPU memory/OOM cannot be confirmed or ruled out from CloudWatch metrics in this environment. To close this gap, the CloudWatch agent's EFA metrics section would need to be enabled (efa_retrans_timeout_events, efa_rx_dropped, etc.) or on-node fi_info/rdma diagnostics collected directly.

# Mitigation Summary

## Action
Purchase an available p6-b300.48xlarge Capacity Block (offering cb-0665692176570d9f8, us-west-2b) and bind the distributed-training-triage-b200 Slurm GPU queue to it, since the cluster's existing reserved slot (cr-0580a9d7420fd589a) is fully consumed by an unrelated verification workload and has no extension offering. In parallel, fix the Capacity Block lifecycle monitoring and CloudWatch log-delivery gaps that hid the fleet loss.

## Reasoning
Training throughput on distributed-training-triage-b200 (VPC vpc-0028c20959269e96f, head node i-01bbde10b04dd4ca8) dropped to zero over 2026-09-28T04:08Z→2026-10-01T04:08Z because the cluster had NO GPU compute nodes. Its prior p6-b300.48xlarge workers (i-0be6193831c898671, i-0014ff22f2e2f180f) terminated at 2026-09-27T11:00:00Z — the classic Capacity Block termination signature. The only active p6-b300 Capacity Block, cr-0580a9d7420fd589a (TotalInstanceCount=1, AvailableInstanceCount=0, active until 2026-10-03T11:30Z), is fully consumed by an unrelated node i-0ec31e7eff7635265 (tags Name=b300-xid-verify, Purpose=PR112-blackwell-verification) in a different VPC (vpc-0968395d1c4c18fbc). There are no extension offerings for cr-0580a9d7420fd589a, but a purchasable p6-b300.48xlarge offering (cb-0665692176570d9f8, us-west-2b, StartDate 2026-10-02T11:30Z, EndDate 2026-10-03T11:30Z, UpfrontFee $2695.68 USD) exists in the same AZ. Storage, GPU hardware, and NCCL/NVLink/EFA were all ruled out as the cause.

### Step 1: Pre Validate

#### 1.1 Confirm the cluster's existing reserved p6-b300 slot is still fully…

```
**Purpose:** Confirm the cluster's existing reserved p6-b300 slot is still fully consumed before buying more capacity.
**Advisory:** If AvailableInstanceCount has since become 1, the cluster may be able to reacquire this slot without a new purchase — re-evaluate before buying.

#### 1.2 Re-confirm the purchasable p6-b300.48xlarge offering in us-west-2b is…

```
**Purpose:** Re-confirm the purchasable p6-b300.48xlarge offering in us-west-2b is still available immediately before purchase.
**Advisory:** Capacity Block offering IDs rotate; use the current ID returned here rather than a stale one.

```
**Purpose:** Confirm the training cluster still has no GPU compute nodes before applying the mitigation.

### Step 2: Apply

#### 2.1 Provision additional p6-b300.48xlarge reserved GPU capacity in…
**Type:** command

```
**Purpose:** Provision additional p6-b300.48xlarge reserved GPU capacity in us-west-2b without touching the unrelated verification workload.
**Risks:** The upfront fee (~$2695.68 USD) is charged immediately and cannot be cancelled or refunded., This block is only usable from 2026-10-02T11:30Z to 2026-10-03T11:30Z (~24h) — a short bridge; pair it with a longer follow-on block for sustained training.
**Advisory:** If no suitable short-duration offering remains, request a longer-duration p6-b300.48xlarge block in us-west-2b.

#### 2.2 Bind the Slurm compute resource to the newly purchased Capacity Block…
**Type:** text
Edit the ParallelCluster config for distributed-training-triage-b200 so the GPU compute resource has CapacityReservationTarget.CapacityReservationId = <new CapacityReservationId> and CapacityType: CAPACITY_BLOCK, then apply with: pcluster update-cluster --cluster-name distributed-training-triage-b200 --cluster-configuration <updated-config.yaml> --region us-west-2
**Purpose:** Bind the Slurm compute resource to the newly purchased Capacity Block so the scheduler launches GPU workers into usable reserved capacity.
**Risks:** The update may require stopping the compute fleet first (pcluster update-compute-fleet --status STOP_REQUESTED); safe here since no GPU workers are currently running., The cluster's exact pre-existing capacity binding was not readable during the investigation — verify the live config before editing.
**Advisory:** Confirm the compute resource's subnet is in us-west-2b to match the block's AZ.

### Step 3: Post Validate

#### 3.1 Confirm the newly purchased reservation exists and track its state…
**Type:** command
```

```
**Purpose:** Confirm the newly purchased reservation exists and track its state toward active.

#### 3.2 Confirm GPU worker node(s) actually launch into the training cluster…
**Type:** command
```
aws ec2 describe-instances --filters Name=vpc-id,Values=vpc-0028c20959269e96f Name=instance-type,Values=p6-b300.48xlarge Name=instance-state-name,Values=pending,running --region us-west-2
```
**Purpose:** Confirm GPU worker node(s) actually launch into the training cluster VPC and reach running once the block is active.
**Advisory:** If no workers launch, inspect Slurm clustermgtd/slurmctld logs — but note those are currently not being delivered; restore log delivery first.

#### 4.1 Provide a clean revert of the configuration change if the capacity…
**Type:** text
Revert the ParallelCluster config to its pre-change state via: pcluster update-cluster --cluster-name distributed-training-triage-b200 --cluster-configuration <pre-change-config.yaml> --region us-west-2. The purchased Capacity Block cannot be cancelled or refunded; if unused it simply expires at 2026-10-03T11:30Z.
**Purpose:** Provide a clean revert of the configuration change if the capacity binding does not produce healthy GPU workers.
**Risks:** The upfront Capacity Block fee is non-recoverable regardless of rollback.

#### 1. Bind the Slurm GPU queue to a dedicated Capacity Block and make lifecycle + logging durable in the cluster definition
**Description:** In the ParallelCluster config for distributed-training-triage-b200, set the GPU compute resource's CapacityReservationTarget to a reservation dedicated to this cluster (not shared with unrelated verification workloads) with CapacityType: CAPACITY_BLOCK, matching subnet AZ to the block's AZ (us-west-2b). - GPU worker kernel/NCCL/EFA logs appear in /aws/fsx-training/distributed-training-triage-b200/kernel and /gpu-health with hourly coverage while a worker runs.
- A Capacity Block Expiration Warning EventBridge rule exists and delivers to an ops notification target.

     15	metadata:
     16	  author: nzuresh
     17	  version: "1.0.3"
     18	  aws-devops-agent-skills.agent-types: "Incident RCA, Chat tasks"
     19	  aws-devops-agent-skills.aws-services: "Amazon SageMaker HyperPod, AWS ParallelCluster, Amazon EC2, Amazon FSx for Lustre, Elastic Fabric Adapter, Amazon EKS, AWS Health"
     20	  aws-devops-agent-skills.technical-domains: "Machine Learning, GenAI, High Performance Computing"
     21	---
     22	
     23	# GPU Cluster Evidence, Readiness, and Fault Verdicts
     24	
     25	For GPU clusters on SageMaker HyperPod (Slurm or EKS), AWS ParallelCluster, and self-managed
     26	EC2 or EKS. Generic investigation finds the obvious signals; this skill adds what it gets
     27	wrong: silent evidence, wrong-headline hardware verdicts, and predictable failures before a
     28	long run. **Read-only.** Never reboot, replace, update, or delete anything, and never read
     29	training data, checkpoints, or model weights.
     30	
     31	## Critical rules R1 to R10 (apply in every mode, in this order)
     32	
     33	R1. **Answer in one pass, and always leave room to answer.** In chat, do not stop to ask a
     34	   question and do not hand off to a separate investigation before answering. If an input is
     35	   missing, use the default (impact window: last 24 hours; run length: evaluate 24, 48, and
     36	   72 hours), state the assumption, and mark dependent checks `Needs input`. For "slow" or
     37	   performance questions with no time given, use the last 72 hours. Offer follow-ups only
     38	   after the answer.
     39	   **Budget the evidence gathering so the answer always gets written.** An investigation that
     40	   runs out of room before it reports is worth nothing to the operator, and it is worse than a
     41	   partial answer because it looks like a failure rather than a finding. So: collect the
     42	   mandatory evidence for the mode first (R2, R4, R5, and for Mode P the P1 to P6 core), then
     43	   write the report. Pick up the optional checks only with what is left. If you notice you are
     44	   deep into tool calls and have not yet produced an answer, **stop collecting and report what
     45	   you have**, marking everything unreached as `Not checked` with the call that would close
     46	   it. Never end a turn with evidence gathered and no verdict.
     47	R2. **Inventory and capability profile.** HyperPod: `sagemaker.DescribeCluster` and
     48	   `ListClusterNodes` (paginate). Read `NodeProvisioningMode` from `DescribeCluster`: if it is
     49	   `Continuous`, also pull `sagemaker.ListClusterEvents` for the window (see rule R11), which
     50	   is the only timeline source that survives broken log delivery. On any other value the call
     51	   is unsupported and must be skipped, not retried.
     52	   EC2/ParallelCluster/EKS: `ec2.DescribeInstances`. For every
     53	   GPU instance type: `ec2.DescribeInstanceTypes` (strip HyperPod `ml.`): GPU count,
     54	   `EfaSupported`, `MaximumEfaInterfaces`; per EC2 node, attached `efa`/`efa-only` interfaces.
     55	   Report `<attached> of <max>`, where attached = interfaces with `InterfaceType` `efa` or
     56	   `efa-only` (the primary ENA interface does not count unless it is `efa`). HyperPod nodes
     57	   are not visible to `DescribeInstances`: say so. On NVSwitch types, search every log source
     58	   found under rule R4 for `Started "Nvidia Fabric Manager"` before saying it is not confirmed.
     59	R3. **Node identity survives replacement.** A HyperPod reboot keeps the instance ID; a replace
     60	   gives the node a **new instance ID in the same instance group**, so the current ID will
     61	   never appear in the replace request. Query CloudTrail **by event name, not by instance
     62	   ID**: `cloudtrail.LookupEvents` with `LookupAttributes=[{AttributeKey: EventName,
     63	   AttributeValue: BatchReplaceClusterNodes}]`, then again for `BatchRebootClusterNodes`,
     64	   `BatchDeleteClusterNodes`, and `UpdateCluster`, with `StartTime` = window start minus 6
     65	   hours and `EndTime` = now as full ISO-8601 UTC timestamps, paginating with `NextToken`.
     66	   Keep events whose `requestParameters.clusterName` is this cluster. A `nodeIds` entry
     67	   that is not in the current `ListClusterNodes` output was replaced; the instance group
     68	   whose node has a `LaunchTime` just after that event is the replaced group. That operator
     69	   or automatic call is the explanation for the node going `Pending` (Branch E), not hardware.
     70	R4. **Find every log source by substring, not prefix.** Call `logs.DescribeLogGroups` with
     71	   `logGroupNamePattern` (case-sensitive substring) = the cluster name, then again for
     72	   `kernel`, `messages`, `syslog`, `journal`, and `gpu`, paginating with `nextToken`. Never
     73	   search only `/aws/parallelcluster` or `/aws/sagemaker` prefixes: customer pipelines use
     74	   other names (for example `/aws/<pipeline>/<cluster>/kernel`). Evaluate every source found.
     75	R5. **Prove coverage before any "no errors".** For each node and source: find the stream that
     76	   carries `kernel:` lines, then bin **that exact stream** by hour across the window padded by
     77	   one hour. **Always name the evidence you used: quote the full log group name and the exact
     78	   log stream name for every node in the coverage table, and again in the answer text.** A
     79	   coverage claim without the group and stream it rests on is not auditable, so the operator
     80	   cannot re-run it. Any empty hour means `Not observable` for that hour. First and last event times
     81	   are not proof, and the time of the **last `kernel:` line** is not when logging stopped:
     82	   a healthy kernel goes quiet. Liveness comes only from the hourly bins of all lines in
     83	   that stream. A node is `Measured` if one source passes. HyperPod: a missing
     84	   `SagemakerHealthMonitoringAgent/<group>/<instance-id>` stream means `No HMA detections`
     85	   when the cluster log group is otherwise live. NCCL transport with no `NCCL INFO` lines
     86	   anywhere is `Not observable`; never infer it from the instance type.
     87	R5a. **Name every resource you looked at, by ID.** A finding the operator cannot re-run is
     88	   not a finding. Whatever you analysed, put its identifier in the answer: the FSx file system
     89	   (`fs-...`) behind any storage claim, the instance IDs (`i-...`) behind any node claim, the
     90	   cluster name, the capacity reservation (`cr-...`) behind any capacity claim, and the log
     91	   group and stream behind any log claim as R5 already requires. "The file system was
     92	   saturated" or "the metrics looked fine" names nothing and cannot be checked. This applies
     93	   to the resource you cleared as much as the one you blamed, since ruling something out is
     94	   only useful if the reader knows what was ruled out.
     95	R6. **Verdict per node, headline to match.** `REPLACE`, `REBOOT`, `LEAVE ALONE`, `MONITOR`, or
     96	   `NOT OBSERVABLE`, against the evidence bar in `references/incident-branches.md` (Step 4b).
     97	   Application-class Xids (for example 13, 31) or HMA `reason: XidUserAppError` with the node
     98	   `Running` is `LEAVE ALONE`. Never headline "hardware error" unless the verdict is `REPLACE`
     99	   or `REBOOT` on hardware grounds.
     100	R7. **Label every cause** `Proven` (measured signal on the affected node, before the failure,
     101	   nothing competing) or `Hypothesis (to validate)` with the one confirming measurement. A
     102	   spike at the same time is correlation. FSx without a saturated metric is not a proven cause.
     103	   Only a `Proven` cause may be called the root cause, in the headline or in a branch table.
     104	   Otherwise write `Leading hypothesis: <cause>`, or `Root cause: Not observable` when the
     105	   deciding evidence is missing (for example a dead control-plane log). Never write "Proven
     106	   mechanism" for something whose trigger or removal path you did not observe.
     107	   Utilization metrics from FSx (`NetworkThroughputUtilization`, `DiskIopsUtilization`, and
     108	   similar) and `GPUPowerUtilization` are already percent from 0 to 100: a value of `0.9` is
     109	   0.9 percent. Quote the raw value with a percent sign.
     110	R8. **Recovery questions** always state three things: whether automatic node recovery is on
     111	   (`NodeRecovery`), what it does (reboot or replace the node), and that the **job** resumes
     112	   only with checkpoints plus the orchestrator's auto-resume (Slurm on HyperPod:
     113	   `srun --auto-resume=1`).
     114	R9. **Capacity Blocks** begin terminating instances 30 minutes before the end time (60 for
     115	   UltraServers); blocks end at 11:30 UTC and termination starts at 11:00 UTC on the last day.
     116	   For a planned run, write out: usable until = end time minus the lead time; run end = start
     117	   plus run length; hours covered = usable until minus start. Give every value as a full UTC
     118	   date and time, and check the latest safe start is not already in the past.
     119	R10. **Rule out the frequent non-GPU causes** in `references/cluster-edge-cases.md` before
     120	   blaming hardware: subnet IP or network interface exhaustion, ParallelCluster bootstrap
     121	   failures and protected mode, EFA nodes in a public subnet, a Capacity Block not yet
     122	   active, and the FSx maintenance window. HyperPod does not export system metrics to
     123	   CloudWatch, so HyperPod GPU activity is `Not observable` there.
     124	R11. **When the logs are dead, ask the control plane.** On a HyperPod cluster with
     125	   `NodeProvisioningMode = Continuous`, `sagemaker.ListClusterEvents` gives you a node and
     126	   cluster timeline that owes nothing to a log agent, so it keeps answering when a stream has
     127	   gone silent or a node has disappeared. Filter the window with `EventTimeAfter` and
     128	   `EventTimeBefore`, narrow with `NodeId` or `InstanceGroupName`, sort with
     129	   `SortBy=EventTime`, and page through `NextToken`. Where a `Description` is not
     130	   self-explanatory, `DescribeClusterEvent` has the detail. Note that the response has no
     131	   severity or level field at all, so any grouping you apply is your own and should be
     132	   described that way. If `NodeProvisioningMode` is anything other than `Continuous` the call
     133	   is not supported; write `ListClusterEvents not supported` in the coverage table and carry
     134	   on. What you must not do is report a dead log as "no events" without either trying this
     135	   source or saying it was unavailable.
     136	
     137	## Pick the mode
     138	
     139	| The user asks | Mode | Steps to run |
     140	|---------------|------|--------------|
     141	| Something failed, hung, slowed, or lost nodes | **I: Incident** | Steps 1 to 7 |
     142	| "Were there GPU errors?", "Can I trust the logs?" | **C: Coverage audit** | Steps 1 to 3, then 6 and 7 |
     143	| "Is the cluster ready for a long run?", Capacity Block ending | **P: Pre-flight** | Steps 1 to 3, then 5P, 6 and 7 |
     144	
     145	## Workflow checklist
     146	
     147	Work through these in order and tick each one as it completes. Skip only the steps the
     148	mode table excludes. Every step below has a matching `## Step N` section with its detail.
     149	
     150	- [ ] Step 1: Scope the request: account, region, cluster or instance IDs, impact window
     151	- [ ] Step 2: Build the inventory, capability profile, and one ordered timeline
     152	- [ ] Step 3: Prove GPU log coverage per node before looking for errors
     153	- [ ] Step 4: Classify each fault and give every node a verdict
     154	- [ ] Step 5: Pull metrics and settle the root-cause branch
     155	- [ ] Step 5P: Score pre-flight checks P1 to P16 (Mode P only, replaces Steps 4 and 5)
     156	- [ ] Step 6: Write the report in the required format
     157	- [ ] Step 7: Self-check the finished output, then present it
     158	
     159	## Step 1: Scope
     160	
     161	Account, region, cluster name or instance IDs, workload, impact window (default last 24 hours,
     162	stated). Classify the symptom to pick a starting branch (Step 5), but collect evidence for all.
     163	
     164	## Step 2: Inventory and timeline
     165	
     166	Load [references/inventory-and-timeline.md](references/inventory-and-timeline.md) for the
     167	inventory API calls and the eight timeline sources, and
     168	[references/cluster-edge-cases.md](references/cluster-edge-cases.md) for the frequent non-GPU
     169	causes to rule out under rule R10:
     170	
     171	```
     172	read_skill_resource(skill_id="aiml-gpu-training-cluster-investigation", path="references/inventory-and-timeline.md")
     173	read_skill_resource(skill_id="aiml-gpu-training-cluster-investigation", path="references/cluster-edge-cases.md")
     174	```
     175	
     176	Build one ordered timeline for the window plus 30 minutes each side: node state, HMA
     177	detections, Xids, AWS Health, EC2 status and scheduled events, Capacity Block and training plan
     178	end times, and CloudTrail cluster changes (rule R3).
     179	
     180	## Step 3: Coverage audit
     181	
     182	Load [references/coverage-audit.md](references/coverage-audit.md) for the log-source discovery
     183	and hourly coverage queries, and
     184	[references/nccl-nvlink-efa.md](references/nccl-nvlink-efa.md) for NCCL transport, NVLink and
     185	NVSwitch, and EFA signals:
     186	
     187	```
     188	read_skill_resource(skill_id="aiml-gpu-training-cluster-investigation", path="references/coverage-audit.md")
     189	read_skill_resource(skill_id="aiml-gpu-training-cluster-investigation", path="references/nccl-nvlink-efa.md")
     190	```
     191	
     192	Produce the coverage table and the node capability and fabric table for every affected node.
     193	Every row names the full log group name and the exact log stream name that row's verdict rests
     194	on, so the operator can re-run the same query. Where no stream carries kernel lines, say which
     195	groups you searched and that none did.
     196	
     197	## Step 4: Classify faults and give node verdicts
     198	
     199	Load [references/xid-triage.md](references/xid-triage.md) for the Xid catalog and per-code
     200	verdicts, and [references/incident-branches.md](references/incident-branches.md) for the node
     201	verdict evidence bar and branches A to F:
     202	
     203	```
     204	read_skill_resource(skill_id="aiml-gpu-training-cluster-investigation", path="references/xid-triage.md")
     205	read_skill_resource(skill_id="aiml-gpu-training-cluster-investigation", path="references/incident-branches.md")
     206	```
     207	
     208	## Step 5: Metrics and root-cause branch
     209	
     210	Load [references/signals-and-thresholds.md](references/signals-and-thresholds.md) for metric
     211	names, dimensions, and thresholds:
     212	
     213	```
     214	read_skill_resource(skill_id="aiml-gpu-training-cluster-investigation", path="references/signals-and-thresholds.md")
     215	```
     216	
     217	Pull FSx (correct dimensions per metric), GPU activity (`AWS/EC2` `GPUPowerUtilization`, unit
     218	Percent, or `CWAgent`), and EFA counters, then evaluate branches A (hardware), B (capacity
     219	lifecycle), C (storage), D (NCCL, NVLink/NVSwitch, EFA), E (cluster change), and F (application,
     220	only after A to E are ruled out), as defined in `incident-branches.md`. Recommend operator
     221	actions only.
     222	
     223	## Step 5P: Pre-flight readiness (Mode P)
     224	
     225	Load [references/preflight.md](references/preflight.md) for pre-flight checks P1 to P16:
     226	
     227	```
     228	read_skill_resource(skill_id="aiml-gpu-training-cluster-investigation", path="references/preflight.md")
     229	```
     230	
     231	Score checks P1 to P16. Lead with FAIL, then RISK. In Mode P this step replaces
     232	Steps 4 and 5.
     233	
     234	**Work the core first, then extend.** All sixteen checks together cost more tool calls than
     235	a single answer usually has room for, and a readiness question with no verdict is a failed
     236	answer however much evidence sits behind it (see R1). So run them in two passes.
     237	
     238	The core, which decides whether the run can start at all:
     239	
     240	| Check | Question it settles |
     241	|-------|---------------------|
     242	| P1 | Does the Capacity Block or training plan outlast the run? |
     243	| P2 | Is there an extension, if it does not? |
     244	| P3 | Is there a spare node to replace a failure? |
     245	| P4 | Is `NodeRecovery` on? |
     246	| P5 | Are deep health checks enabled? |
     247	| P6 | Is GPU error logging arriving, so a failure during the run is visible? |
     248	
     249	Write the readiness verdict as soon as those six are scored. P7 to P16 then refine it, and
     250	each one you reach can only add a `RISK`, never change a `FAIL` already found in the core.
     251	Anything you do not reach is reported `Not checked` with the call that would settle it, which
     252	is an honest answer; silence is not. If the core itself is incomplete, say which part and
     253	give the verdict you can support.
     254	
     255	## Step 6: Report
     256	
     257	Load [references/report-format.md](references/report-format.md) for the report template and its rules:
     258	
     259	```
     260	read_skill_resource(skill_id="aiml-gpu-training-cluster-investigation", path="references/report-format.md")
     261	```
     262	
     263	## Step 7: Self-check before presenting
     264	
     265	Before showing the answer to the user, re-read your own draft and verify each of these.
     266	Fix the draft where a check fails; do not present an output that fails one.
     267	
     268	- [ ] Every "no errors found" statement is backed by a node whose coverage you proved in
     269	      Step 3. If coverage was not proven, the wording is `Not observable`, not healthy.
     270	- [ ] Every coverage row names its full log group and exact log stream (rule R5). A coverage
     271	      claim with no named source is not auditable and must be fixed before presenting.
     272	- [ ] Every node verdict still meets the evidence bar that justifies it, re-read from
     273	      [references/incident-branches.md](references/incident-branches.md) Step 4b.
     274	- [ ] The headline matches the verdicts. It does not say "hardware error" unless a verdict
     275	      is `REPLACE` or `REBOOT` on hardware grounds (rule R6).
     276	- [ ] Every cause carries a `Proven` or `Hypothesis (to validate)` label, and anything
     277	      labelled `Proven` has a measured signal on the affected node before the failure
     278	      (rule R7). Nothing unproven is called the root cause.
     279	- [ ] Every percentage came straight from the metric without rescaling (rule R7).
     280	- [ ] Every absent signal is reported as `Not observable` with what to collect, never as
     281	      zero or as healthy.
     282	- [ ] Each recommendation names an operator action, and no mutating API call was made.
     283	- [ ] Every number in the answer can be traced to a call you actually made this run.
     284	- [ ] Every resource you analysed appears by ID (rule R5a): the `fs-...` behind a storage
     285	      claim, the `i-...` behind a node claim, the `cr-...` behind a capacity claim, the
     286	      cluster name, the log group and stream. This holds for resources you cleared, not just
     287	      the one you blamed.
     288	- [ ] **There is an actual answer.** A verdict or root cause is written down, not just
     289	      evidence. If you ran out of room before finishing, the draft still leads with the
     290	      verdict you can support and marks the rest `Not checked` (rule R1).
     291	
     292	State the outcome of this self-check in one line, naming anything you could not verify.
     293	
     294	## Success criteria
     295	
     296	- Coverage table and node capability table for every affected node; no "no errors" without
     297	  proven coverage.
     298	- One verdict per node with a GPU signal; headline consistent with the verdicts.
     299	- Every cause labelled `Proven` or `Hypothesis (to validate)`.
     300	- Replaced nodes matched to the operator or automatic action that replaced them.
     301	- Mode P: P1 to P16 scored.
     302	- No mutating API call was made.

{"id": "3ec2cdde-8bb9-428c-a621-37265d73ca0c", "role": "user", "content": [{"text": "IMPORTANT: Respond entirely in English (observations, findings, summaries). Technical terms, resource names, and ARNs stay in their original form.

The file system is DeploymentType SCRATCH_2, StorageCapacity 1200 GiB SSD, StorageType SSD, FileSystemTypeVersion 2.15. Note: a SCRATCH_2 at 1200 GiB has a limited aggregate throughput ceiling (~200 MB/s per TiB), so saturation is plausible.

Investigative question: Is FSx for Lustre fs-077c776983688ad76 saturated or otherwise degraded in a way that would throttle the training job's dataset reads during the window 2026-09-28T04:08Z to 2026-10-01T04:08Z?

Load the skill aiml-gpu-training-cluster-investigation and read references/signals-and-thresholds.md for the exact FSx metric names, dimensions, statistics, and flagging thresholds. Also load the exploring-metrics skill for CloudWatch query mechanics.

Pull these AWS/FSx CloudWatch metrics for fs-077c776983688ad76 across the full 72h window (use a period that reveals sustained saturation, e.g. 300s, and also look at daily rollups to see the trend over the "last few days"):
- NetworkThroughputUtilization (dimensions FileSystemId + FileServer), stat Maximum — flag >= 90% sustained 5+ min. THIS IS THE KEY SATURATION METRIC.
- FileServerDiskThroughputUtilization (FileSystemId + FileServer), Maximum — flag >= 90% sustained 5+ min.
- CPUUtilization for the metadata server (FileSystemId + FileServer where FileServer begins MDS*), Maximum — flag >= 90% (metadata server saturation).
- MetadataOperations (FileSystemId), Sum/period — look for a sharp rise aligned with the slowdown.
- DataReadBytes and DataWriteBytes (FileSystemId), Sum/period — convert to bytes/sec (Sum / period_seconds); characterize the read throughput the clients are achieving and whether it changed over the window.
- FreeDataStorageCapacity (FileSystemId, StorageTargetId), Minimum per OST — flag any OST < 10% free.
- Note: DiskIopsUtilization does not apply to Scratch; skip or note if empty.

CRITICAL per the skill (R7): FSx utilization metrics (NetworkThroughputUtilization, FileServerDiskThroughputUtilization, DiskIopsUtilization) are already a percentage from 0-100 — a value of 0.9 means 0.9%, NOT 90%. Quote the raw value with a percent sign. A drop in DataReadBytes is usually the EFFECT of a stalled job, not a cause — it only points to storage if a saturation metric rose first.

Analysis goals:
- Establish whether any FSx saturation metric reached >= 90% and sustained it, and WHEN (does it align with "the last few days" trend of declining throughput?).
- Characterize the achieved read throughput (DataReadBytes rate) across the window and whether it rose to a ceiling or declined.
- Compare the earlier part of the window (a healthier baseline, e.g. 2026-09-28) against the most recent part (2026-09-30 to 2026-10-01).

{"id": "db13136b-98da-47cb-bf5f-5316364c1c77", "role": "user", "content": [{"id": "tooluse_pwSMD73i51h9ERzF2TvYkw", "content": [{"text": "     1	---
     2	name: aiml-gpu-training-cluster-investigation
     3	description: Use this skill for GPU training or inference clusters on SageMaker HyperPod (Slurm or
     4	  EKS), ParallelCluster, or self-managed EC2/EKS GPU instances. It adds three things.
     5	  First, a GPU evidence coverage audit that proves per node whether kernel Xid logs and
     6	  HyperPod health-agent detections were actually arriving, hour by hour, so "no errors
     7	  found" is never reported from a silent log. Second, a node verdict (replace, reboot,
     8	  or leave alone) against an explicit evidence bar, so an application Xid is never
     9	  headlined as hardware. Third, a pre-flight readiness check before a long run, covering
     10	  Capacity Block or training plan end time versus run length, spare capacity to replace
     11	  a failed node, NodeRecovery, deep health checks, EFA, log coverage, idle reserved
     12	  GPUs. Activate on Xid or ECC errors, slow training or FSx for Lustre slowness on a GPU
     13	  cluster, NCCL hangs or TCP fallback, NVLink or Fabric Manager errors, nodes in Failure
     14	  or Pending, nodes terminating at once, or "is my cluster ready for a multi-day run".
     15	metadata:
     16	  author: nzuresh
     17	  version: "1.0.3"
     18	  aws-devops-agent-skills.agent-types: "Incident RCA, Chat tasks"
     19	  aws-devops-agent-skills.aws-services: "Amazon SageMaker HyperPod, AWS ParallelCluster, Amazon EC2, Amazon FSx for Lustre, Elastic Fabric Adapter, Amazon EKS, AWS Health"
     20	  aws-devops-agent-skills.technical-domains: "Machine Learning, GenAI, High Performance Computing"
     21	---
     22	
     23	# GPU Cluster Evidence, Readiness, and Fault Verdicts
     24	
     25	For GPU clusters on SageMaker HyperPod (Slurm or EKS), AWS ParallelCluster, and self-managed
     26	EC2 or EKS. Generic investigation finds the obvious signals; this skill adds what it gets
     27	wrong: silent evidence, wrong-headline hardware verdicts, and predictable failures before a
     28	long run. **Read-only.** Never reboot, replace, update, or delete anything, and never read
     29	training data, checkpoints, or model weights.
     30	
     31	## Critical rules R1 to R10 (apply in every mode, in this order)
     32	
     33	R1. **Answer in one pass, and always leave room to answer.** In chat, do not stop to ask a
     34	   question and do not hand off to a separate investigation before answering. If an input is
     35	   missing, use the default (impact window: last 24 hours; run length: evaluate 24, 48, and
     36	   72 hours), state the assumption, and mark dependent checks `Needs input`. For "slow" or
     37	   performance questions with no time given, use the last 72 hours. Offer follow-ups only
     38	   after the answer.
     39	   **Budget the evidence gathering so the answer always gets written.** An investigation that
     40	   runs out of room before it reports is worth nothing to the operator, and it is worse than a
     41	   partial answer because it looks like a failure rather than a finding. So: collect the
     42	   mandatory evidence for the mode first (R2, R4, R5, and for Mode P the P1 to P6 core), then
     43	   write the report. Pick up the optional checks only with what is left. If you notice you are
     44	   deep into tool calls and have not yet produced an answer, **stop collecting and report what
     45	   you have**, marking everything unreached as `Not checked` with the call that would close
     46	   it. Never end a turn with evidence gathered and no verdict.
     47	R2. **Inventory and capability profile.** HyperPod: `sagemaker.DescribeCluster` and
     48	   `ListClusterNodes` (paginate). Read `NodeProvisioningMode` from `DescribeCluster`: if it is
     49	   `Continuous`, also pull `sagemaker.ListClusterEvents` for the window (see rule R11), which
     50	   is the only timeline source that survives broken log delivery. On any other value the call
     51	   is unsupported and must be skipped, not retried.
     52	   EC2/ParallelCluster/EKS: `ec2.DescribeInstances`. For every
     53	   GPU instance type: `ec2.DescribeInstanceTypes` (strip HyperPod `ml.`): GPU count,
     54	   `EfaSupported`, `MaximumEfaInterfaces`; per EC2 node, attached `efa`/`efa-only` interfaces.
     55	   Report `<attached> of <max>`, where attached = interfaces with `InterfaceType` `efa` or
     56	   `efa-only` (the primary ENA interface does not count unless it is `efa`). HyperPod nodes
     57	   are not visible to `DescribeInstances`: say so. On NVSwitch types, search every log source
     58	   found under rule R4 for `Started "Nvidia Fabric Manager"` before saying it is not confirmed.
     59	R3. **Node identity survives replacement.** A HyperPod reboot keeps the instance ID; a replace

     2	name: aiml-gpu-training-cluster-investigation
     3	description: Use this skill for GPU training or inference clusters on SageMaker HyperPod (Slurm or
     4	  EKS), ParallelCluster, or self-managed EC2/EKS GPU instances. It adds three things.
     5	  First, a GPU evidence coverage audit that proves per node whether kernel Xid logs and

     8	  or leave alone) against an explicit evidence bar, so an application Xid is never
     9	  headlined as hardware. Third, a pre-flight readiness check before a long run, covering
     10	  Capacity Block or training plan end time versus run length, spare capacity to replace
     11	  a failed node, NodeRecovery, deep health checks, EFA, log coverage, idle reserved
     12	  GPUs. Activate on Xid or ECC errors, slow training or FSx for Lustre slowness on a GPU
     13	  cluster, NCCL hangs or TCP fallback, NVLink or Fabric Manager errors, nodes in Failure
